title: Tensor pairing of frames under ordinary pullback
statement: For any morphism f:X to T of schemes [def-pc-scheme], module sheaves L,M on T [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and maps x:f*O to f*L, y:f*O to f*M, define their tensor frame as f*(lambda inverse), followed by the inverse monoidal tensor comparison on the unit, x tensor y, and the monoidal comparison on L,M. This construction is invertible for invertible x,y. It commutes with composition of scheme pullbacks and with the pullback of global maps. Scaling either input by a global section r of O_X scales the output by r. The construction agrees with the expression using the canonical pullback unit isomorphism, by strong monoidal left unitality [lem-pc-scheme-pullback-monoidal-existing].

source.place: Lemma tensor-product-pullback (Tag 01CD); existing source pullback tensor-composition and monoidal-unit comparison theorems, Tags 0095 and 0096.

proof.text: Define the tensor pairing by the ordinary pullback monoidal comparison; all factors are isomorphisms when the input maps are, so the pairing is too. Monoidal naturality cancels the two tensor comparisons for global maps.

For composition of two strong monoidal functors, tensor compatibility of the comparison isomorphism gives compatibility of its inverse by cancellation. Naturality with the unit splitting and the two input maps proves the tensor pairing composition equation. Specialize to ordinary scheme pullback using its proved tensor composition equation.

A scalar endomorphism commutes with every module map by linearity. On pure tensors, multiplying either factor by r equals multiplying the tensor by r. The tensor sheafification universal property extends this equality to all sections. Move this scalar through the unit splitting to obtain the two scalar equations.

Write presheaf restriction on the over-category explicitly as the module pseudofunctor pullHom, simplifying op-unop before comparing types. The composition formula gives compatibility of tensor frames with pullHom. Compatibility of pullHom with composition of module maps and its formula on a global mapped morphism give the presheaf pairing equation and the restricted-global-map equation.

theorem tensorPullbackFrames_comp {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) (g : Z ⟶ Y)
    (L M : X.Modules)
    (x : (Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj (Scheme.Modules.unit X) ⟶
      (Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj L)
    (y : (Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj (Scheme.Modules.unit X) ⟶
      (Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj M) :
    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g f).inv.app (Scheme.Modules.unit X) ≫
      (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).map
        (tensorPullbackFrames L M f x y) ≫
      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g f).hom.app (L ⊗ M) =
    tensorPullbackFrames L M (g ≫ f)
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g f).inv.app (Scheme.Modules.unit X) ≫
        (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).map x ≫ (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g f).hom.app L)
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g f).inv.app (Scheme.Modules.unit X) ≫
        (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).map y ≫ (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g f).hom.app M)
